## Body

**Performance: pass-with-notes** at `af50381aafd734a57d0ae169821788e38a37314f`.

Reviewed fixes `702b73c`, `5127ee0` and test-only `af50381`, plus their integration with #141's view. Main's four merge commits are not independently re-reviewed. The earlier performance verdict at `3ecec77f46ac335e6fe141ecf75baf5637378e7b` otherwise stands. No new executable launch site, independent timer, polling task or automatic model wake from these fixes.

| Surface | Cost and limits |
|---|---|
| Admission gates | The existing short synchronous map lock still only finds/creates an async gate keyed by `(project, role)` (`community/directory.rs:166-234`). All instances of that role serialize together; unrelated keys have separate gates. Entries remain unevicted for the daemon lifetime. Draining now acquires the gate for each request and holds it through existing claim, admission/delivery and settlement (`delivery/role_send.rs:776-814`), releasing it between requests. This adds async wait/serialization, not a process or spin loop. |
| Cancelled waiters | Inserts and withdrawals move the guard into the existing owned-write task; retire/merge moves it into the existing blocking writer job and returns it after commit (`store/role_requests.rs:189-207,334-350`; `directory.rs:1871-1889`). The wrappers do not add a second task or transaction. Caller cancellation intentionally no longer frees admission while independently owned work can still land. |
| **Latency qualification** | Retire/merge can hold a role gate while queued for the blocking pool or shared writer lock, during role/routes preparation, validation, git staging/commit, pointer indexing, route notification, per-request withdrawal notices and withdrawal. Concurrent sends and drains for that role inherit this latency. The gate does not impose a new whole-operation deadline or backlog bound. Existing component timeouts/retries are not an end-to-end cap; CI tests gate lifetime, not contended production latency. |
| New delivering read | Each retire/merge attempt, including a withdrawal resume, adds `delivering_for_role` before the queued read (`directory.rs:898-922`). This is a conservative brake: it can refuse retirement while a claim could return to the queue; it does not cause retirement. The forced delivering index is keyed only by `created_at` (`0034_role_requests.sql:33-34`), not project/role. Work can scan the global delivering population before filtering. Returned matching rows are unpaged and include bodies, though the refusal only formats metadata. No EXPLAIN or live cardinality measurement was made. |
| Routes regeneration | Edit/retire/merge now call the existing `routes::regenerate` inside the same writer callback (`directory.rs:1019-1021,1163-1165`). It reads/parses all role documents once, clones the parsed inventory, builds before/after tables, compares rows and reads the old markdown (`routes.rs:290-340`). Memory follows combined parsed documents and route/overlap results. Existing dedup/diff membership scans and pairwise path-overlap checks can be quadratic in route/path counts. This extra CPU/file work happens under the shared writer lock, and under the role gate for retire/merge. |
| Commit and notification | Changed `ROUTES.md` is added to that same write with `document: false`: no extra commit or ddocs validation/build for markdown. The nominal direct writer budget remains 7 + 2D invocations, D = validated documents, excluding contention retries and executable descendants. A changed table additionally uses the existing project/prime lookup and holds one FYI for a live prime; it does not wake a model. Unchanged rows skip that notification. Resume still skips the writer/regeneration and retains its existing per-request notice/withdrawal work. |
| Prime picture integration | The view reads each role document once into a retained vector and derives standings from it (`directory.rs:307-321`). Retired roles are excluded from actions, scope ownership, idle review and call-on, but still pay listing/history and memory-freshness work. Peak memory retains all parsed role documents, not just the current role. Active-role queued-instance matching retains P141-N001's scaling limit. Offering retire/merge as command strings adds no automatic execution or clock. |

**Proof:** this exact head is CLEAN. [CI 42365297866](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42365297866) has all four jobs successful; the latest [delivers run 42365593363](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42365593363) also succeeds. Rust JUnit lists **2,076 executed cases, zero failures/errors**, including drain/retirement exclusion, cancelled-waiter gate lifetime, delivery recovery/refusal, withdrawal resume, quoted-instance repair, edit/retire routes, retire/merge history, updated prime view/command replay and all six spawn guards. Five Rust tests were skipped separately.

No local builds, tests, mutation runs, runtime probes or review-tree changes. Reviewer/security own their finding closure and authority analysis; this is the cost verdict.
